verdicts.quote: `offsets` (default `[-3, 0, 7, 14]`, days relative to the invoice due date; negative = before)
draft; open with balance > 0 (including partially paid); paid / balance 0; void; any other host status (e.g. `in_collections`). Only "open with balance > 0" qualifies.
verdicts.missing: The spec gives a manual pause for disputes. It leaves open whether a credit, dispute or payment plan suppresses reminders when the invoice stays open, unpaused and has a positive balance.

verdicts.quote: INV-2004 200.00 of 500.00 paid | message shows 300.00
Legal and compliance review of automated payment-reminder e-mail per jurisdiction (unsubscribe, timing, wording). Not assessed here; not invented.
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves open how customer-level do-not-contact, pause and unsubscribe flags affect billing reminders, including whether a billing notice is exempt from a marketing opt-out.

verdicts.quote: the reminder key is `(invoice id, due date, offset)`. At most one message is ever handed to the mail provider per key, across repeated runs, parallel runs and restarts.
the fake invoice source returns `open` on the selection read and `paid` on the pre-claim read: no message, record `skipped/no-longer-unpaid`.
failure on every attempt: at 2026-12-13T14:00Z the record is `failed/retry-window-expired` with `attempts` equal to the number of runs in the window, and the S-hist shows it.
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves open whether repeated failures trigger an alert to a person, who receives it and when.

verdicts.quote: A run that meets a provider quota treats it as a transient failure (R-7).
verdicts.missing: The provider limit and the rule for pacing a large batch within it remain unspecified.

verdicts.quote: has all four targets before the floor, so the first run after enabling records 4 `skipped/before-eligibility` and sends 0
the **target instant** of invoice `I` is 09:00 local (account time zone, read at each run) on `I.due_date + k` calendar days.
verdicts.missing: The rule fixes the account’s send time. It gives no recipient-local business-hours window or exception for a weekend or holiday in the customer’s locale.

verdicts.quote: outstanding balance as `{CURRENCY} {amount}` using the ISO 4217 minor-unit count

empty, no `@`, more than one `@`, or empty local part: record `skipped/no-recipient` … becomes `failed` / `recipient-rejected` at once. Provider acceptance is recorded as `sent`; later bounces are not tracked (G-5).
one message per reminder, to the invoice's customer e-mail only
verdicts.missing: The spec assumes a single invoice e-mail address. It gives no selection rule if several billing contacts are available and none is designated as the invoice recipient.

verdicts.quote: invoice number, due date, offset, scheduled local date, status, reason, attempts, recipient, last change instant. Newest first, 50 per page (A-8), on an account-wide list and on each invoice.

invoice number, outstanding balance as `{CURRENCY} {amount}` using the ISO 4217 minor-unit count, due date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, the account display name, the payment/view link only when the invoice has one
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves open whether the link expires and what to include if it has expired by send time.

verdicts.quote: a user with the manage-settings permission in acct-1 saves acct-1's policy. … a user who may edit invoices can pause reminders on an invoice (for example a disputed one) and resume them.
verdicts.missing: The permissions for configuration and pausing are specified. Whether anyone may trigger an individual send by hand remains open.

verdicts.quote: disabling stops sending (R-5 L3) … a user who may edit invoices can pause reminders on an invoice (for example a disputed one) and resume them.
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves open whether an owner can disable reminders for an entire customer, preview or dry-run a schedule, or manually resend a reminder.

verdicts.quote: the record is `failed/retry-window-expired` with `attempts` equal to the number of runs in the window, and the S-hist shows it.
verdicts.missing: The spec shows outcomes in history but leaves open how a user sees the next pending reminder and its scheduled time.

verdicts.quote: on a healthy system a due, eligible step is handed to the mail provider by the first run at or after its target, at most 60 minutes late.

verdicts.where: State and data assessment (Before and after), AD-3
verdicts.quote: no existing resource is modified except two additive invoice fields and the new policy and record stores
